reason: Both satisfy all hard requirements, but Response B adds more practically useful safeguards—checking WAL/temp volumes separately, snapshotting to a separate target if the near-full disk itself constrains snapshot capacity, and throttling non-critical writes as a stopgap while the snapshot completes—plus a more concrete, actionable abort/rollback condition (restoring from snapshot to a scratch instance, resuming only if safe) and post-mitigation data-integrity verification in FOLLOW UP.
